marking_points.point: Software insecurity stems from an attacker's ability to modify system resources critical for program execution, such as instruction pointers or function call addresses.
marking_points.quote: Software insecurity stems from attacker's ability to modify system resources criticial for program execution, e.g. instruction pointer, function call addresses, interrupt addresses, etc.

marking_points.point: One of the key sources for software insecurity is failed validation of user input.
marking_points.quote: One of the key sources for software insecurity is failed validation of user input.

marking_points.point: Buffer overflows are a most widely used exploitation technique against software.
marking_points.quote: Buffer overﬂows are a most widely used exploitation technique.

marking_points.point: Without proper bound checking, a buffer content can overspill into adjacent upper stack area.
marking_points.quote: Without proper bound checking a buffer content can overspill into adjacent upper stack area.

marking_points.point: By controlling buffer content, an attacker can overwrite the return address with an arbitrary value and hijack the execution flow.
marking_points.quote: By controlling buffer content, an attacker can overwrite the return address with an arbitrary value and hijack the execution ﬂow.

marking_points.point: Active Directory is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources including users, groups, security credentials, and security policies that govern the application's environment.

questions.question: State six distinct malware attack techniques or propagation methods used to compromise computer systems.

marking_points.point: Boot sector infection, where a program spreads by infecting the boot sector of storage media.
marking_points.quote: A program spread via boot sector infection

marking_points.point: Exploiting debugging features of network services such as sendmail for remote execution to propagate across networks.
marking_points.quote: Used a debugging feature of sendmail (remote execution)

marking_points.point: Appending a virus body to an executable COM program and replacing its entry point with a jump to the virus code.
marking_points.quote: Replace a program entry point                                   with a jump to a virus body

marking_points.point: Overwriting an EXE program header to switch the entry point to the virus body.
marking_points.quote: Over write a program header to switch the entry point to a virus

marking_points.point: Self-replication in shared memory environments to increase survival chances against competing programs.
marking_points.quote: To increase their survival chances, programs can replicate themselves

marking_points.point: Injecting malicious Javascript into a user profile so that any visitor's page becomes infected and propagates the script further.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

questions.question: Discuss six preventive network security mechanisms and related protection strategies that an organization can deploy to secure its infrastructure.

marking_points.point: Remote Access VPN is a preventive mechanism that provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) enforces the principle that a user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role.
marking_points.quote: A user                                              should only has access and permission that                                            required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) are deployed to detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security                                                  attacks such as brute force attacks,                                                          Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of                                                 network vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) uses a combination of technology and best practices to prevent the exposure of sensitive information outside oof an organization.
marking_points.quote: Combination of technology and best practices to prevent the exposure of sensitive information outside oof an organization.

marking_points.point: Email Security encompasses any processes, products and services designed to protect email accounts and email contents from external threats.
marking_points.quote: Any processes, products and services                                                   designed to protect email accounts and email                                         contents from external threats.

marking_points.point: Sandboxing provides a safe, protected and isolated environment in computer system to run or open suspected insecure programs or files.
marking_points.quote: A safe, protected and isolated environment in                                       computer system to run or open suspected                                            insecure programs or files.

questions.question: Explain the fundamental mechanism of a substitution cipher and identify the cryptographic principle to which it corresponds.

marking_points.point: In a substitution cipher, plain-text letters are replaced with other letters to produce the cipher-text.
marking_points.quote: In substitution ciphers, we replace the plain-text letters with other letters

marking_points.point: This substitution technique corresponds to Shannon's principle of confusion.
marking_points.quote: Corresponds to Shannon’s principle                                          of confusion

questions.question: Discuss six characteristics, advantages, or disadvantages of specific biometric technologies and categories used for authentication.

marking_points.point: Biometrics are defined as physiological or behavioural human characteristics that can distinguish one person from another for identification or verification purposes.
marking_points.quote: “A biometric is a physiological or behavioural characteristic of a human being that can distinguish one person from another and that theoretically can be used for identification or verification of identity.”

marking_points.point: Biometric applications are categorized into psychological sectors such as iris, fingerprints, hand, retinal, and face recognition.
marking_points.quote: Psychological: Iris, Fingerprints, Hand, Retinal and Face recognition

marking_points.point: Behavioural biometric categories include voice recognition, typing pattern analysis, and signature verification.
marking_points.quote: Behavioural: Voice, Typing pattern, Signature

marking_points.point: Fingerprint biometric systems have the disadvantage that they can be spoofed, making liveness detection important.
marking_points.quote: Can be spoofed – liveness                                              important!

marking_points.point: Retinal scanning is considered very efficient because it cannot be spoofed by an attacker.
marking_points.quote: Very efficient – cant be spoofed!

marking_points.point: Iris recognition technology overcomes several issues associated with retinal scanners and does not require physical touch.
marking_points.quote: Overcomes retinal scanner                                        issues

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Discuss six aspects of the Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attack technique, including its underlying vulnerability, propagation mechanism, and impact on victims, as illustrated by self-propagating malware such as the Samy worm.

marking_points.point: The fundamental vulnerability enabling XSS worms is that any web application returning user input without filtering becomes exploitable.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

marking_points.point: XSS attacks propagate by allowing the execution of arbitrary Javascript code directly within the victim's browser environment.
marking_points.quote: Allows execution of arbitrary Javascript in user’s browser.

marking_points.point: Unlike normal scripting, XSS involves malicious Javascript that does not originate from the trusted web server but is dynamically injected via a user request.
marking_points.quote: In a XSS attack, Javascript does not originate from a web server but is dynamically injected  into it via a user request

marking_points.point: An attacker initiates the infection chain by using one of the website's forms to insert a malicious string into the website's database.
marking_points.quote: The attacker uses one of the website's forms  to insert a malicious string into the website's database.

marking_points.point: When a victim requests the compromised page, their browser executes the script and sends the victim's cookies to the attacker's server.
marking_points.quote: The victim's browser executes the malicious script inside the response, sending the victim's cookies to the attacker's server.

marking_points.point: Script injection techniques such as XSS are formally classified as significant software threats alongside other code injection methods.
marking_points.quote: Script injection (e.g. XSS)

questions.question: Describe six characteristics of the access control matrix, access control lists, and capability structures used to implement access policies.

marking_points.point: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies, including the access control matrix (ACM), capabilities (C-List), and access control lists (ACL).
marking_points.quote: Access control structures are mechanisms for implementing access policies: access control matrix (ACM) Capabilities (C-List) access control lists (ACL)

marking_points.point: The access control matrix (ACM) serves as a basic control structure that offers clarity of definition and is easy to verify.
marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure. Advantages: clarity of deﬁnition easy to verify

marking_points.point: An ACL provides an object-centered description of access rights, mapping each object to the subjects permitted to access it and their allowed operations.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights:

marking_points.point: A disadvantage of using ACLs is the poor overview of access rights per subject, along with difficulty of revocation and sharing.
marking_points.quote: Disadvantages: poor overview of access rights per subject difﬁculty of revocation difﬁculty of sharing

marking_points.point: In practical systems such as Windows, a DACL in a security descriptor is implemented as a list of Access Control Entries (ACE) containing principal SIDs and access rights masks.
marking_points.quote: DACL in a security descriptor is a list of Access Control Entries (ACE)

marking_points.point: Access rights within these structures describe what one can do to an object and are often encoded as a bit mask, including standard rights like DELETE and READ_CONTROL.
marking_points.quote: Describe what one can do to an object Encoded as a 32-bit mask Standard access rights: common to most object types

questions.question: Describe six distinct threat classes or countermeasures relevant to computer security, covering vulnerabilities, attacks, preventive mechanisms, and detection system capabilities.

marking_points.point: A vulnerability is a weakness of a system that can be exploited by threats to damage assets.
marking_points.quote: Vulnerabilities: Weakness of a system that can be exploited to damage assets

marking_points.point: An attack represents the actual violation of security, as opposed to a potential threat.
marking_points.quote: Attacks: The actual                                                                               violation of security

marking_points.point: Prevention countermeasures include technical instruments such as vulnerability scanning and software updates.
marking_points.quote: Prevention: vulnerability scanning, software updates

marking_points.point: Firewalls act as preventive network security mechanisms that control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Intrusion detection systems provide near real-time detection and response to identified attacks.
marking_points.quote: Near real-time detection and response

marking_points.point: Passive detection systems serve as a countermeasure class that can take passive action (logging and alerting) when an attack is identified but cannot stop it in progress.
marking_points.quote: Can take passive action (logging and alerting) when an attack is identified

questions.question: State six characteristics or functions of the components that make up the Next Generation Secure Computing Base (NGSCB) architecture.

marking_points.point: The NGSCB architecture is built upon two primary system components, namely Nexus and the Nexus Computing Agent (NCA).
marking_points.quote:
Two primary system components
Nexus
Special kernel (core of the trusted operating)
Goal:  Isolate the process of  normal mode and                                                  trusted mode                                                                                differently in memory
Functionality: Authenticate and protect data                                                    (entered, stored, communicated, and                                                             displayed) by data encryption
Nexus Computing Agent (NCA)

marking_points.point: Nexus acts as a special kernel forming the core of the trusted operating environment.
marking_points.quote:
Nexus
Special kernel (core of the trusted operating)

marking_points.point: A key goal of the Nexus component is to isolate the processes of normal mode and trusted mode differently in memory.
marking_points.quote: Goal:  Isolate the process of  normal mode and                                                  trusted mode                                                                                differently in memory

marking_points.point: Nexus provides functionality to authenticate and protect data entered, stored, communicated, and displayed by using data encryption.
marking_points.quote: Functionality: Authenticate and protect data                                                    (entered, stored, communicated, and                                                             displayed) by data encryption

marking_points.point: Nexus operates as a security kernel that is authenticated on boot and serves as an application interface to the TPM without trusting the OS.
marking_points.quote:
Security kernel, authenticated on boot
Authenticates trusted programs
Application interface to TPM
Does not trust OS

marking_points.point: The Nexus Computing Agent (NCA) is a trusted software component that runs in trusted mode and communicates directly with Nexus.
marking_points.quote:
Trusted software component
Runs in trusted mode that communicates with Nexus

questions.question: Explain six aspects of Kerberos, smartcards, and Single Sign-On (SSO) mechanisms used for authentication in computer systems.

marking_points.point: Single Sign-On is motivated by the need to reduce the need to memorize passwords across multiple services.
marking_points.quote: Reduce the need to memorize passwords

marking_points.point: Client-server architectures such as Kerberos and Active Directory serve as solutions for implementing Single Sign-On.
marking_points.quote: Client-server architectures (Kerberos, Active Directory)

marking_points.point: During a Kerberos user login, the hash value of the user's password becomes a secret key of the client or user.
marking_points.quote: The hash value of his password                                                      KU = h(P) becomes a secret key of the                                                  client/user.

marking_points.point: Single sign-on methods such as Kerberos provide means for automating authentication in large distributed environments.
marking_points.quote: Single sign-on methods such as Kerberos provide means for automating authentication in large distributed environments.

marking_points.point: Smart cards are recognized as an alternative user authentication mechanism alongside biometric methods and two-factor authentication.
marking_points.quote: Alternative user authentication mechanisms are smart cards, biometric methods and two-factor authentication.

marking_points.point: In Windows security architecture, Kerberos was introduced as a key security milestone starting with Windows 2000.
marking_points.quote: Windows 2000: Active Directory, Kerberos, security architecture.

questions.question: Explain six professional conduct and ethical obligations that a computing professional must uphold according to established codes of ethics such as the ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct.

marking_points.point: Ethics is defined as a documented set of acceptable behaviors for professional or social groups, which forms the basis of any professional code.
marking_points.quote: Documented set of acceptable behaviors for professional or social groups.

marking_points.point: Professional organizations such as the Association of Computing Machinery (ACM) have established a formal code of ethics and professional conduct to guide practitioners.
marking_points.quote: Association of Computing Machinery ACM (founded 1947) has a code of ethics and professional conduct.

marking_points.point: Under the ACM Code of Ethics, a computing professional should contribute to society and to human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.
marking_points.quote: Contribute to society and to human well-being, acknowledging that all people are stakeholders in computing.

marking_points.point: The ACM Code of Ethics requires professionals to respect privacy and honor confidentiality as core ethical duties.
marking_points.quote: Respect privacy.

marking_points.point: Regarding professional conduct, a computing professional should strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.
marking_points.quote: Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.

marking_points.point: Professionals are also obligated to design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure, directly linking ethical conduct to computer security practice.
marking_points.quote: Design and implement systems that are robustly and usably secure.
